title: A family in Brussels
body: Pieter's family speaks Dutch and lives in Brussels, where most residents speak French. Pieter's parents want to know which authority decides matters about Dutch-language schooling, cultural centres and the use of Dutch in education for their community. A neighbour tells them that the Brussels government decides everything in the city, while another says that only the Central Government in Belgium can decide such questions. Pieter's teacher explains that Belgium has an unusual arrangement: besides the Central Government and the State Governments of the regions, there is a third kind of government that is organised around language communities rather than territory.
